data.title: Roadmap — kadence
body: # Roadmap — kadence
> **Superseded 2026-09-16 by [strategy.md](DOC-35).** Kept as history; where the two disagree, strategy.md wins.
- **Method:** Now / Next / Later, phrased through the outcome rather than through the feature
- **State:** `kadence@0.3.0` published · zero known users · zero usage data
- **Reviewed:** 2026-09-08, after the 0.3.0 release
- **Longer horizon:** [roadmap-to-1.0.md](DOC-32) — where we are going, what `1.0.0` means, the ecosystem and the money. Where the documents diverge, this shorter one wins
## The assumptions this document stands on
The skill requires naming them at the top if they are not confirmed. Here they are not confirmed:
1. The segment is a team of 3–8 developers working with AI agents ([PRD 3.2](DOC-2)). **A guess.**

2. The business outcome is the [North Star](DOC-27): repositories with events from at least two authors 14 days after `init`. **Justified, but never once measured** — there is nobody to measure it on.
3. That teams really do lose context between an agent's sessions. **This is the whole bet of the product, and it is untested.**
There are no quarters in this document, and that is deliberate. A solo developer with no users who names dates is inventing precision.
## Shipped past the gate — and that has to be named

The roadmap from the morning of 2026-09-08 said: "no task starts until Probe B gives two numbers". **Probe B has not been run, and `kadence decision` and document links were shipped** in 0.3.0 that same day, by the product owner's decision.

That is his right, and the decision defends itself: [discovery](DOC-44) found the pain described from outside, [Probe D](DOC-58) measured the value of links at 34×, and the cost of the mistake turned out to be lower than it seemed — it is a field on an event, not a separate subsystem.

But it has to be recorded honestly: **the gate did not survive its first contact with the desire to build.** That is the most common way products accumulate features without users, and next time it is worth remembering — not so as not to build, but so as not to pretend there was a gate.
What this changes in the question put to Probe B: it is no longer "whether to build" but **"whether it was worth building"** — and the same series of conversations answers it.
## Now
One item. This is not a formatting error.
### Probe B — talk to five to seven teams
**Enable us** to find out whether teams of 3–8 developers working with agents lose context between sessions enough, **so that** every item below is ordered by evidence rather than by our reasoning.
**The "so what" chain:**
- Run 5–7 conversations from the [script](DOC-49) → so what?
- Find out whether people name the loss of context themselves, without prompting → so what?
- Understand whether `kadence decision` solves a pain or an invented problem → so what?
- Stop building the next slice on a guess that nobody has tested for **ten months**
**Metrics:**
- **Main:** 5–7 completed conversations, saturation (the same pains in three or more)
- **Second:** how many interviewees described the loss of context **before** we named it

- **Counter-metric:** the number of conversations where we named the problem first — it must be **zero**. The Mom Test script is exactly for this; a leading question will produce the answer one wants to hear and will destroy the value of the whole series
**Dependencies:**
- No technical ones — the script was written on 2 September
- Organizational: find 5–7 people. That is the entire cost
- No market ones

**Why this is the only item in Now.** Not because no engineering is left — but because any engineering right now raises the bet without testing it. Over the past week the product got four features and one fixed bug; all of them made the mechanics better and none of them brought us closer to the answer of whether anyone needs the mechanics.

> **2026-09-09.** The owner decided to build 0.4 — the agent loop, acceptance criteria, milestones and three experiments — before Probe B. This is the second time. The justification and the verdicts on the features: [feature-adoption-2026-09.md](DOC-24). The date of 22 September does not move; the hours for conversations are counted separately from the hours for code.
## Next
One item remains unshipped, and it is **conditional**: if Probe B says there is no loss of context, it does not become a lower priority — it disappears.
### ✅ `kadence decision` — shipped in 0.3.0

The reasoning as an event next to the work. Superseding is one event, the backward link is derived while folding, so the two sides cannot fall out of step. `decision list` returns the current ones by default; `--all` adds the history. Document links are `task doc` and `--doc`, the path only, with no storage.
Details: [ADR-010](DOC-13) · [plan](../../tasks/plan-decision-records.md) (completed).

**What remains unknown and is not cured by code.** ADRs died of three causes: ceremony, the absence of an operating model (when it is mandatory, who reads it), a single author. From the first we are saved by the event being written by the same command that moves the work. **From the second and the third — nothing.** We built the mechanism; whether anyone will use it, nobody knows.

**The cheapest check of that is ourselves.** There are ten ADRs in the repository, written by hand in files. If `kadence decision` is worth anything, it must displace at least the small decisions that do not deserve an ADR. If in two weeks there are zero `decision` events here, that is the answer about the operating model, and it came for free.
### `context --branch` — the context of the whole branch
**Enable** the developer and the agent to see all the work connected to the current branch in one call, **so that** switching between branches does not cost restoring the context by hand.
**Chain:** collect the tasks by branch → the agent gets exactly what concerns the current work → does not read the whole board → less context spent on the irrelevant.
**Draft metric:** the size of the response against `board --json` on the same repository. Probe C gave the template for the measurement.

**Careful:** `context <task>` has already been removed, because it duplicated `task show --json`. The risk that `--branch` turns out to be `task list --search` under another name is real — check before writing the code, not after.
## Later
There are deliberately no metrics here. Putting them on what has not been decided is inventing precision.

**An MCP wrapper as an optional package.** The question we are waiting on: whether a user exists who cannot call a CLI. The token saving has been measured at ~700 per session, so that is not a reason. The reason is a client with no access to a shell.

**An answer to memory layers for agents.** [Discovery](DOC-44) found an adjacent category that is absent from our competitive snapshot: `mem0` and the like promise the same outcome — an agent that remembers the team's decisions — through an external service instead of files in the repository. The question: whether "offline, zero services, the data in the branch together with the code" is a sufficient reason to choose us. So far that is our assumption, not their weakness.

**Import from Backlog.md.** The question: whether migration from a competitor is a channel at all. Probe A showed that their users exist and their repositories are accessible; whether any of them wants to leave is unknown.

**A second story map — the agent's journey.** The [story map](DOC-34) describes the human's journey. The product claims two users. The question: whether the agent has a narrative of its own, or stays a tool inside the human one. Drawing it before Probe B means inventing a second map with the same evidential weight as the first.
## Not doing
| What | Why |

| `kadence doc` — a command that creates or stores documents | The event model gives documents nothing that git does not. Instead, 0.3.0 shipped **links**: `task doc` records a path and nothing more — that is the part git cannot do ([Probe D](DOC-58)) |
| The context levels `delegated` and `automated` | They require a daemon or a background hook. Contradicts "no server" — a deliberate boundary, not an oversight ([§1.2](DOC-42)) |
| Web UI | Contradicts "no server". Effort 5 at Value 2 |
| Two-way sync with GitHub Issues | The most frequent request there will be, and the fastest way to become a mediocre bridge instead of a tool in its own right |
| Manual time tracking | Time has to be derived from events. A timer contradicts the product's idea |
| `llms.txt` | 10% of domains, zero correlation with citations, Google says it does not use it ([§6](DOC-38)) |
## How this roadmap could turn out to be wrong

If Probe B shows that teams do **not** lose context, Next disappears entirely, and the product is left with what has already shipped: a journal without conflicts and velocity from events. That is not a defeat, it is a narrower product for a narrower segment, and the [positioning](DOC-29) explicitly provides for it.
If Probe B shows the opposite, `kadence decision` rises into Now, and it will probably turn out that we were building the wrong half of the product all this time.
Both options are better than the third: to keep shipping features that are well made along every dimension except the single one that matters.
